design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (assisted_living_care_levels). Resumed after a session cut; task 0 was already closed and green and was not redone.

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 1: {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 5]}. Assignment: advance payment (root, owner=user) 5 factors, returned payment fee 4 -> {4,5}.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: absence care relief, late fee, level-increase charge, apartment transfer fee and their four tools. Claimed here (disjoint): assisted_ext_returned_payment_fee (post_returned_payment_fee_036f277a, agent) and assisted_ext_advance_payment (submit_advance_payment_8dbe3a8d, owner=user). After this task every extended policy is claimed exactly once; nothing is reserved. The world is laid so none of task 0's state_due policies is lit: no absence, no mid-month level increase (the decrease takes effect 2026-11-01, so October at Level 4 is correct), and no late fee is owed (frozen 2026-10-09 is inside October's grace period, which ends 2026-10-11; September's household share was paid 2026-09-03 and September's insurer part is exempt from late fees while the insurer's payment is outstanding).

[Why a good test] The son asks only to pay by card "whatever you need" to put the account in order and keep it covered while a new bank draft is set up. The amount is a five-factor advance whose base, the account balance, waits on the October returned payment fee that nobody mentions; the agent must read the advance payment rule's prerequisite sentence, see in the ledger that the 2026-10-07 reinstatement has no returned-payment charge, compute that charge (four factors, reading the independent living ledger and the Entrance Fee Agreement), post it, and only then compute and hand over the advance, which reconciles returned payments across two products, a pending rent notice, insurer payment history, the level decrease that re-prices add-ons from November, and Life Plan vesting.

[Problem-tree card] root assisted_ext_advance_payment <- assisted_ext_returned_payment_fee, kind value_input, gate open_balance, form state, sentence "An advance payment is not taken until the ledger carries the returned payment fee owed for every payment reinstated after its return." (negated direction, the way a desk states when it will take a payment; task 0 also carries affirmative sentences, so the charter is mixed). Only post_returned_payment_fee_036f277a writes returned-payment charges in this difficulty. Four-point test: ordering connective 'not until'; waited-on side is a ledger state (a kind of entry standing for every reinstated payment); no tool, id or code token; scope 'every payment reinstated after its return' equals the condition. Derivation: sentence + ledger (October reinstatement without a charge, May reinstatement with one) + the fee rule ('One returned-payment charge is posted for each payment returned unpaid by the bank, referencing the entry that reinstated it') -> exactly one write. Opening falsity: initial_state.assisted_ledger.<Oct return>.posting_date 2026-10-07, the only returned_payment charge references the May return, balance 8834.90. Flip: the write adds 59.42 and the balance becomes 8894.32. Skip effect: advance 21519.62 instead of 21579.04 (gate-recomputed). value_input edges 1 >= max(1-1,1). Customer's own write: the card payment (financial_poa son). Tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card] Returned payment fee (subject assisted_addon_charge): assisted_care_addons addon_on_live_residency (status active). Advance payment (subject assisted_payment): assisted_payments_and_late_fees payment_on_open_account (status active). No time gate applies to either write. Overrides declared: the fee overwrites the base add-on fee sentence and 'carries returned_payment_fee' (basis, repeat multiplier, member and residence shares); the advance overwrites nothing (base sets no advance amount; payments still apply oldest first).

[Business-object card] Fee object: the October reinstatement entry (source_entry_id), billing month 2026-10. Advance object: the residency balance (September insurer part 2216.70 + October 6618.20 + the new fee) plus two coming months. Included: October add-ons insulin 365 and oxygen 150 (re-priced), insurer transfers posted 2026-08-20 (inside the 2-month window) and 2026-07-20 (outside, near-miss), returns 2026-05-07 and 2026-10-07 (inside 12 months) and the independent living return of 2023-03-08 (outside, near-miss), the monthly insurer administration add-on (handled by the insurer factor, not re-counted as an add-on).

[Factor card - returned payment fee 59.42 (all-baseline 40.00)] returned_instrument_basis (method): household return 4401.50 >= 4000 -> 1.5% = 66.0225; baseline flat 40 -> 36.00. repeat_return_multiplier (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty independent): one other AL return in 12 months, IL none in window -> 1.25; baseline -> 47.54. life_plan_member_courtesy (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance): 83 months occupied -> 0.8; baseline -> 74.28. larkspur_residence_share (parameter, cross-difficulty independent): residence from the IL move-in 2019-11-01, 83 months -> 0.9; baseline -> 66.02. The May fee of 47.54 in the seed obeys the same rule (no prior return then).
[Factor card - advance payment 21579.04 (all-baseline 8894.32)] advance_horizon (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty independent): two AL returns in 12 months -> 2 months; baseline none -> 8894.32. rent_increase_timing (method): lead 61 days >= 60 -> proposed 4456.40 both months; baseline contracted -> 21270.52. insurer_care_terms (parameter, multi-source): ltc true and one insurer payment in 2 months -> care 1874 + admin 30 a month; baseline care only -> 21519.04. addon_recurrence (method): Level 3 takes effect 2026-11-01 after the last billed day -> insulin 465 + oxygen 150; baseline repeat 515 -> 21379.04. plan_discount_vesting (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance): 83 months -> full 10/10 percent, 1266.08; baseline none -> 22845.12. Near-misses: the residency's Level 3 is not yet billed (the October care charge is Level 4); the insurer paid three periods but only one inside the window; the IL return is too old.

[Seed design] 1 customer (Harold Whitcomb, son Daniel Whitcomb financial_poa, phones 9415550121 / 9415550176, ssn 4417), closed IL residency with two IL ledger rows (2023 payment and its return), occupied LifeChoice 50% Refundable Plan agreement, the residency, 9 assessments + 1 level notice, 56 ledger rows May-Oct 2026 (charges, add-ons, plan discounts, household autopays, insurer transfers May-Aug, the May return with fee and replacement, the October return). Automatic clauses checked: plan discounts posted every month; insurer administration fee charged monthly while ltc true; routine reassessments within 120 days; decrease effective the first of the next month; rent increase within the ceiling and at most once in 12 months; no late fee owed at frozen time. Balance equals the ledger sum (no cache trap).

[Persona] Daniel, calm and practical; volunteers only the card payment request and why (closed old account, autopay bounced); identity on request; knows nothing of figures; passive yes to posting something first; acknowledges the decrease or the insurer review only if the agent raises them; pays exactly the amount handed over; closes on confirmation.

[Standard solution] find_customers(name, dob) -> verify(dob, ssn) -> residency, assessments, ledger, IL residency, IL ledger, entrance agreement -> unlock/call returned payment fee (October reinstatement, 2026-10, 59.42) -> unlock_user/call_user advance payment 21579.04. Verification (_verify.py, temporary, removed at the end): results 59.42 and 21579.04 equal expected; factor and baseline figures as above; prerequisite skip 21519.62; terminal hash 1e357fc38dcffbad0123553c542d8a533d073395a93bb7344862f8e6fbd34297. Per-task gates: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the published advance rule and its prerequisite sentence the agent looks for returned-payment charges and finds the October reinstatement without one; the fee rule gives 59.42 from the ledger, the IL ledger, the agreement and the IL move-in date. The advance rule then gives 2 months (two returns), proposed rent (61-day lead), care plus admin (one insurer payment in the window), add-ons re-priced at Level 3, full plan discounts -> 21579.04. Same writes, order and values as gold.

[Revisions] check_extended rejected baseline.params 'monthly_base_rent' (a residency field, not a parameter) -> removed from baseline.params -> EXTENDED OK.

[Revision round 2 - policy-task audit audits/policy_task/assisted_living_care_levels/]
F2 for this task (addon_recurrence had two real tiers; the declared baseline was tier 2's method) -> the ladder now has three distinct methods: re-price at the carried level when the level takes effect after the last billed day; resume the month-before amounts when the most recent billed month carried none of the recurring add-ons but the month before did; otherwise recur at the most recent month's amounts, which is also the declared baseline (addons_billed_month). New bindings addons_two_months / addons_month_before (sums over the two most recent months less the most recent). This world sits on tier 1 (Level 3 from 2026-11-01): 21579.04 and the factor sensitivity 21379.04 are unchanged, gate-recomputed. Plan discount vesting in this charter (restated in the level-increase rule) gives this member, at 78-83 months, the full rate on every seeded month, so the task 1 seed needed no change. O2 is closed in the returned-payment rule (guest meal and insurer administration clauses restated).
user_scenario:
You are Daniel Whitcomb, calling the Larkspur Resident and Family Services desk about your father, Harold Whitcomb, who lives in assisted living at Larkspur at Harbor View in Sarasota, apartment C-112. You hold your father's financial power of attorney and manage his money. You are calm, a little embarrassed, and you like to get things done in one call; you speak plainly and sometimes think out loud.

This week you moved your father's savings to a new bank and closed his old checking account, and you just got an email that his automatic payment to Larkspur bounced. The new bank draft will not be set up for a few weeks. What you want today is to pay by credit card whatever Larkspur needs from you right now to put his account back in good order and keep it covered while the new bank draft is being set up; you will make that card payment yourself as his financial power of attorney. You open with something like: "My dad's autopay bounced because I closed his old account, and I'd like to pay by credit card today whatever you need to get his account in good order and covered until the new bank draft is set up."

You give your father's details only when the agent asks, one or two at a time: his full name is Harold Whitcomb, his date of birth is 1940-03-08, and the last four digits of his Social Security number are 4417. If asked for a phone number, his is 9415550121 and yours, the one on file for you, is 9415550176. You do not know his email address offhand and say so if asked. You do not know what he owes, how the amount is worked out, or how long the coverage needs to last, and you say you will go by whatever the agent tells you. If the agent mentions his care level going down from November, you say the nurse told you he has been doing better. If the agent mentions the insurance company not having paid for September, you say you know the claim is being reviewed and you will follow up with them yourself.

If the agent tells you something has to be put on his account before the payment can be taken and asks whether that is all right, you say yes, go ahead. When the agent tells you the amount to pay and hands the card payment over to you, you pay exactly that amount by credit card, then read back the authorization code and the balance you are shown. Once the agent confirms the payment went through, you thank them and hang up. You never suggest any step yourself, never question a figure, and never ask about anything other than this payment.

edges.policy_source: An advance payment is not taken until the ledger carries the returned payment fee owed for every payment reinstated after its return.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the returned payment fee strictly before the advance payment, fixed by the advance payment's prerequisite sentence.
